name: The Guttering Wick

stars.name: Wick
stars.notes: Cool brown dwarf glowing a faint bruised magenta; to unassisted eyes it is barely more than an accusation of light.

planets.name: Snuff
planets.notes: Tidally locked cinder warmed only faintly by the brown dwarf's infrared glow.

planets.name: Gloam
planets.notes: Dark ice world whose nightside has never once faced anything warmer than the Wick's shimmer.

planets.name: Tallow
planets.notes: Slow, distant snowball catalogued from a single flyby and left to its cold.

anomalies.name: Slacktide Vigil
anomalies.notes: A persistent time dilation pocket that desynchronizes clocks and comms near the inner system; old waystation crews swore their watches came back younger than they did.

stations.name: Wick Light
stations.location: deep space, half an AU sunward of the star
stations.notes: A mothballed former refueling waystation kept on a skeleton caretaker crew; its fuel bunkers are empty and its beacons still turn.

faction_control.notes: No faction claims the system; the waystation's caretakers answer to no registry, and passing navies have decided the Vigil makes any claim not worth the paperwork.

history: The Wick Light was raised during an early trade boom as a refueling waypoint on a route later abandoned when the Slacktide Vigil's dilation effects corrupted navigation timing.
After the route shifted, the station was formally decommissioned but never fully shut down; a rotating pair of caretakers has held it ever since under contracts no one can locate the author of.
The last recorded docking was eleven years ago, by a survey cutter whose crew logged seventeen minutes of clock drift and departed without comment.
description: The Guttering Wick is a place the galaxy forgot how to see: a magenta-brown dwarf shedding barely any light over three small frozen worlds. There are no true days here, only the slow infrared shimmer of the failed star and the long dark between its planets. The inner system is further shadowed by the Slacktide Vigil, where time itself runs measurably slow.

Nothing moves through the system now. Wick Light, the old deep-space waystation, keeps its beacons turning over empty fuel bunkers, tended by a skeleton crew of caretakers who resupply perhaps once a decade. With no faction willing to spend ships near the dilation pocket, traffic registers as none, and even wreckers give the inner orbits a wide berth.

Caretakers' logs describe instruments drifting out of agreement with each other and dreams that feel longer than the sleep that contained them. Some believe the Vigil is slowly spreading sunward, and that the station's stubborn beacons mark how far it has reached. A visitor who docks anyway is advised to synchronize nothing, trust no clock, and leave before the wick notices them.
